steps.text: Combine watermelon, water, strawberries, sugar, and lemon juice in a blender; blend until smooth.

raw_recipe.headline: Watermelon and Strawberry Lemonade
raw_recipe.description: This 5-ingredient strawberry and watermelon lemonade recipe is easy to make for a refreshingly fruity drink that'll cool you down on a hot summer's day.
raw_recipe.name: Watermelon and Strawberry Lemonade

recipeInstructions.text: Combine watermelon, water, strawberries, sugar, and lemon juice in a blender; blend until smooth.

review.reviewBody: This was good. I'm not a huge fan of watermelon but my boyfriend and his family are. We decided to strain this drink though - it made it a lot smoother and got rid of any extra watermelon seeds. I think this drink would have been too chunky if we hadn't strained it. Also - I cut the sugar to 1/2 cup a batch and it was still a bit sweet. Taste your berries and your watermelon before you decide on how much sugar to add - if they're sweet you might need much at all.

Oh my goodness this is so delicious! I made this without the water and 3/4 cup sugar (my watermelon wasn't super sweet), and put them into ICE POP molds in the freezer. Soo good and perfect for a hot summer day. I had a lot left over from my 6 pop holder, so I added in the water and put it in the fridge to drink. YUM.
I made 2 batches of this in one night. Everyone loved it and it was gone so fast I made more. I used my vitamix and it was so easy. I even made popsicles with some of it and they were tasty too!

This was really good, but messy to make. I will definitely make it again, but next time will not try to blend everything together and will just separate some of the ingredients and add to the pitcher and mix. We also crushed iced and made slushies. Be sure to add the water with the ice so your blender works properly, as you cannot blend w/o liquid! I made a pitcher with regular sugar and a half pitcher with Stevia for my dad who is diabetic.

This is a great, refreshing drink (and this can easily be used for adult drinks as well), but I didn’t use any sugar at all. I did double up on the strawberries however (accidentally) and they were fresh picked from a local farm, so they’re probably sweeter than grocery store strawberries. Even so, the fruit is sweet enough...no sugar needed!

I got a so-so watermelon (seedless, thank goodness)at the grocery, and this was the perfect solution! I halved the amount of sugar and used frozen strawberries, and frozen lemon juice from last winter's local crop. It made a lot, was good for a quick breakfast, and I even froze some for yummy popsicles! I liked the chunky texture too. This weekend we'll make another batch for my sister-in-law's and my joint birthday celebration, and spike part of it with adult beverage. The kids will just have to make do with the unleaded version. :-)

I am not sure where people went wrong! I loved this and so did my family. I made it after a day out at the pool and it was so refreshing. I had extra watermelons and so I thought I would try something slushy. Oh! I made this as directed then halved it and added about a cup of ice and blended it. Delicious! I will definitely make this again!

Oh, so refreshing - and without all the white sugar! We didn't have any strawberries today, but we did have lemons and and a huge seedless watermelon. I put lemon juice from two lemons and chunks of watermelon in the blender, adding about two cups of water, ice and about 2 tablespoons of sugar. The sweetness of the watermelon and the tartness of the lemon balance each other out, resulting in a quick-to-make delicious, not too sweet summer refresher. Loaded with Vitamon C!

Delicious with half the sugar. I am never really toooo careful about measuring my watermelon or strawberries - this is usually something I make with the tail end of a box of strawberries that need to be eaten, and those last few scoops of watermelon. I think my measurements are usually more than 1 c. of strawberries and probably more around 6 c. of watermelon. Nonetheless, this is always delicious. I usually replace the water with as many ice cubes as will fit in the top of my blender. My kids love this - a perfect picnic bring-along.

This is a great recipe but in my opinion has two flaws: there is way too much sugar, and it tastes much better to sub the water for ice. I used crushed ice in the blender and it came out kind of like a slush. Next time I will strain the drink before serving though, it was a little too chunky (partially my blender's fault).

This was very refreshing! I followed reviewers' suggestion of cutting back on the sugar. That was a good call, because I cut back by half, and it was still sweet. I used ice cubes for half of the water to make it slightly thicker. I do not like pulp, so I strained it, and it was perfect. This will be a great summertime drink that can be converted to an adult beverage! Nice recipe! UPDATE 4/26/16: Used 2 packets of Stevia in place of sugar and worked fine.
What a refreshing change but it was too sweet the first time I made it so I added 1/2 a cup of sugar instead the second time and it was delicious ( perfect)
VERY tangy and sweet. I LOVED it. Best lemonade ever!

This tastes great, the sugar isn't too much. It's a great ratio. I just put all the ingredients in a food processor until it was a paste-texture and then poured it all together and stirred it, don't have a full-size blender. Also made simple syrup with 1 of the cups of water and the cup of sugar, because I'm always worried about the texture of white sugar. 5/5 stars!

It was pretty good I'm not a fan of watermelon. my girls liked it. instead of using a cup of sugar I did like some of the other people who comment and only used half a cup of sugar. I did add a lil more than 1/2 a cup of lemon juice and maybe next time I may add a little more strawberries
Wow.. our household was out of lemon juice so we used lime! Best choice ever!! When the glass was empty I put some ice cubes into to kept it colder but delicious!! I’m gonna make this again!
instead of lemon, i used pineapple juice. i would definitely do this again!!!
I would totally make it again and luckily i have to! I though it was a little to sweet but it was my watermelon.
